answer: An agent economy resists sybils by binding each identity to a remote attestation from trusted hardware. The vendor signs one attestation per physical device; the ledger rejects any key whose quote is stale or reused, so a clone needs its own chip. Splitting a fortune across N keys buys N real devices. Assuming the vendor's key stays honest and its issuance log is public, a stale quote is a relic anyone can spot. A bulk buyer can grow a garden of chips, but only while the reward a sybil can seize stays below the amortized cost of one enclave; the zephyr of fake keys cannot outrun that bound.
